title: Autonomous AI Leads & People Enrichment Platform
subtitle: B2B Prospecting & Web-Scale Enrichment Engine (WorksBuddy)
summary: Developed a B2B prospecting platform processing 5,000-10,000+ professional profiles using FastAPI, Next.js, Redis, and PostgreSQL/SQLite to collect and organize company, people, and decision-maker information from multiple web sources.

caseStudy.problem: Manual B2B prospecting and decision-maker profile collection is slow, expensive, and frequently hindered by authentication walls, invalid contact emails, and static unstructured web data.
caseStudy.research: Researched headless discovery patterns and DNS deliverability handshakes to engineer a Google SERP-based discovery mechanism that retrieves professional contact data without requiring LinkedIn session authentication.
caseStudy.architecture: A decoupled, asynchronous architecture featuring FastAPI API services, Next.js interface, Redis Streams task queuing, PostgreSQL/SQLite databases, and Groq high-speed LLM inference.
caseStudy.challenges: Managing concurrent background scraping workers, avoiding rate limits, scoring deliverability accurately, and generating personalized outreach hooks in real-time.
caseStudy.solutions: Orchestrated asynchronous background processing with Redis Streams and concurrent workers, configured an email validation system using DNS MX, SPF, DMARC, and SMTP handshake checks, and implemented Groq (Llama/Qwen) workflows for executive summaries and prospect-quality scoring.
caseStudy.performance: Successfully handled 5,000-10,000+ professional profiles with automated deliverability scoring, defensive upserts, deduplication, and CRM synchronization.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Asynchronous event queues (Redis Streams) paired with ultra-low-latency LLMs (Groq) enable resilient, real-time autonomous data enrichment at enterprise scale.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Q&A System (RAG)
subtitle: Multi-Document Q&A Pipeline with Agentic Re-Querying
summary: Constructed an end-to-end RAG pipeline using LangChain, FAISS, and OpenAI/HuggingFace embeddings for semantic question answering across a multi-document corpus with dynamic CrewAI/LangGraph agent orchestration.

caseStudy.problem: Standard semantic search frequently suffers from low precision or returns irrelevant context due to vocabulary mismatch, poor chunking strategies, and ambiguous user prompts.
caseStudy.research: Evaluated document splitters, recursive character chunking boundaries, and vector similarity thresholds across FAISS vector indexes to optimize retrieved context quality.
caseStudy.architecture: FastAPI REST API orchestrating document chunking, embedding generation, FAISS similarity search, and a supervisor agent powered by LangGraph and CrewAI.
caseStudy.challenges: Handling ambiguous queries or out-of-distribution questions without hallucinating incorrect answers or failing to retrieve relevant context.
caseStudy.solutions: Extended the system with CrewAI/LangGraph agent orchestration to dynamically re-query and expand terms against the knowledge base whenever initial retrieval confidence was insufficient.
caseStudy.performance: Maintained retrieval latency under 120ms while resolving 97% of low-confidence or ambiguous queries cleanly through real-time FastAPI endpoints.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Dynamic multi-agent re-querying loops overcome standard semantic search blindspots, drastically improving downstream response reliability.

title: MCP-Based Business Agents — Lio, Taro, Evox & Inzo
subtitle: Multi-Agent Operational Automation & Tool-Calling (WorksBuddy.Ai)
summary: Developed MCP-based AI agents for lead, task, email, and invoice management, integrating business APIs to automate operational processes and execute application-level actions.

caseStudy.problem: Managing leads, client tasks, transactional emails, and invoice creation required human operations across multiple isolated enterprise portals.
caseStudy.research: Adopted the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to standardize context injection, server-client handshakes, and verifiable tool-calling schemas.
caseStudy.architecture: A Python & FastAPI orchestration server exposing MCP tools to four specialized agent personas (Lio, Taro, Evox, Inzo) coordinating state with business databases.
caseStudy.challenges: Ensuring state consistency, robust error recovery during chained API invocations, and preventing unintended tool activations.
caseStudy.solutions: Engineered agent orchestration, tool calling, and context-aware execution with Python and REST APIs, incorporating data synchronization and error handling for reliable backend communication.
caseStudy.performance: Established structured data exchange with third-party services and business systems to maintain consistent application state across interconnected workflows.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Standardizing tools via MCP enables reliable agent autonomy while preserving strict enterprise authorization and auditability.

title: Real-Time Multilingual AI Voice Agent
subtitle: Sub-2s Conversational Voice Pipeline with Persistent Memory (WorksBuddy)
summary: Architected a multilingual conversational system supporting 3 languages using LangGraph with specialized agents for FAQs, knowledge-base queries, and task execution, achieving 1-2 second response latency.

caseStudy.problem: Standard voice conversational pipelines experience 4-6 second response latencies, poor interruption handling, and lack of cross-session customer memory.
caseStudy.research: Analyzed streaming WebRTC protocols (LiveKit) and audio frame processors (Pipecat) to build a low-overhead streaming audio pipeline.
caseStudy.architecture: An asynchronous audio pipeline linking LiveKit and Pipecat to Deepgram STT, routed through LangGraph multi-agent decision controllers, with Mem0 context persistence and ElevenLabs streaming voice synthesis.
caseStudy.challenges: Synchronizing speech recognition, agent tool lookups, and telephony latency over mobile networks.
caseStudy.solutions: Deployed supporting services with Python, FastAPI, Next.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Azure, and Twilio, covering APIs, data persistence, caching, and telephony integration.
caseStudy.performance: Achieved 1-2 second end-to-end response latency for speech recognition, streaming, and voice synthesis across 3 supported languages.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Persistent cross-session memory (Mem0) transforms transactional voice bots into natural, personalized conversational partners.

title: WorksBuddy - Local Document Intelligence & OCR Solution
subtitle: OCR-to-LLM Extraction Pipeline with Zero External API Fees (WorksBuddy)
summary: Reduced manual data-entry effort by ~70% by developing a Document Intelligence solution with PaddleOCR, FastAPI, and locally hosted LLMs (Ollama - Phi-3 / Llama 3.2) for automated extraction from invoices, resumes, and visiting cards.

caseStudy.problem: Manual data-entry from physical and PDF documents (invoices, resumes, visiting cards) is slow and exposes sensitive customer documents to compliance risks on public cloud APIs.
caseStudy.research: Benchmarked OCR engines for coordinate layout preservation, selecting PaddleOCR paired with locally hosted quantized LLMs via Ollama.
caseStudy.architecture: An end-to-end OCR + LLM pipeline built with FastAPI and PaddleOCR, feeding extracted text blocks into Ollama (Phi-3 / Llama 3.2) and enforcing Pydantic schema validation.
caseStudy.challenges: Handling non-standard invoice formatting, skewed smartphone scans, and guaranteeing deterministic JSON outputs.
caseStudy.solutions: Designed an OCR-to-LLM processing workflow to transform unstructured image and PDF content into structured information, enforcing Pydantic schema validation for consistent JSON.
caseStudy.performance: Delivered a privacy-focused REST API for real-time document ingestion using a fully local stack, reducing data-entry effort by ~70% with zero cloud API costs.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Strict schema validation combined with local open-source LLMs provides enterprise document extraction reliability at zero marginal API cost.

title: Student Performance Data Analysis & Academic Risk Modeling
subtitle: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) & Statistical Risk Indicators (JSPIDERS)
summary: Conducted exploratory data analysis (EDA) on student performance datasets using Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn, identifying trends, performance patterns, and academic risk indicators.

caseStudy.problem: Educators lacked quantifiable insights into the socioeconomic and preparatory drivers affecting student test performance.
caseStudy.research: Conducted structured exploratory data analysis across student test scores and demographic attributes to surface meaningful patterns.
caseStudy.architecture: A clean statistical pipeline utilizing Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn for data cleansing, cohort grouping, distribution analysis, and multivariate comparisons.
caseStudy.challenges: Isolating the primary drivers of performance variation across overlapping demographic factors.
caseStudy.solutions: Performed segmented statistical analysis across parental education, test preparation, gender, and lunch type to quantify relationships with student performance and identify key outcome drivers.
caseStudy.performance: Analyzed performance-group differences and identified patterns associated with up to 20% variance in scores, translating findings into data-driven academic recommendations.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Segmented statistical comparisons provide far clearer guidance for targeted educational intervention than aggregate class averages.
